title: O'Reilly: Brown inventions handed to consortium
summary: Jesse Michels tells of O'Reilly: Brown inventions handed to consortium, about mid-20th century at United States (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: He says that a couple of other Brown inventions were handed over to other entities and this consortium seems to have something to do with it.

plain: Townsend Brown was an American inventor of the mid-1900s, described in a documentary by podcast host Jesse Michels as a scientist who built flying-saucer-like devices for the government. Michels relays that a source named O'Reilly says a couple of Brown's other inventions were handed over to outside organisations, and that a group he calls a consortium seems to have something to do with it. If true, it would mean Brown's work was quietly passed to private hands rather than vanishing.
